fields.name: Linear Regression
fields.description: Linear Regression estimates a continuous target variable by fitting a linear relationship between one or more input features and the predicted outcome.
fields.mathematical_foundation: The model minimizes a least-squares objective by finding coefficients that reduce the sum of squared residuals between predictions and observations.
fields.advantages: Easy to interpret, computationally efficient, and effective when feature relationships are close to linear.
fields.disadvantages: Sensitive to outliers, assumes linearity, and may underperform on highly non-linear problems.
fields.applications: House price prediction, demand forecasting, trend estimation, and baseline regression studies.
fields.complexity: Training typically scales with feature count and matrix decomposition cost; inference is linear in the number of features.

fields.name: Decision Tree Classifier
fields.description: Decision Trees recursively partition feature space into regions that maximize class purity according to criteria such as Gini impurity or information gain.
fields.mathematical_foundation: The algorithm greedily chooses splits that optimize impurity reduction until stopping criteria or pruning constraints are reached.
fields.advantages: Highly interpretable, handles mixed data types, and requires little preprocessing.
fields.disadvantages: Can overfit noisy data and may become unstable when data distributions shift slightly.
fields.applications: Medical diagnosis support, credit scoring, customer segmentation, and rule extraction tasks.
fields.complexity: Training depends on the number of candidate splits per level; inference cost is proportional to tree depth.

fields.name: K-Means Clustering
fields.description: K-Means partitions observations into K clusters by iteratively refining centroids and assigning each sample to its nearest centroid.
fields.mathematical_foundation: The objective minimizes the within-cluster sum of squared distances between samples and their assigned centroids.
fields.advantages: Simple, fast on medium-sized datasets, and easy to visualize.
fields.disadvantages: Requires the number of clusters in advance and can converge to local minima depending on initialization.
fields.applications: Market segmentation, document grouping, image compression, and exploratory data analysis.
fields.complexity: Each iteration scales with the number of clusters, samples, and features.
